correctness.rationale: TARGET headline verified independently. C-order = diagonal + {(a^n b,b a^n)} holds globally: bottoms start with 'a', tops with 'b', so sets disjoint and no length>=2 chains; poset reflection trivial, antisymmetry direct. D-order = diagonal + G holds globally for same reason (nonempty top-tuples all b-initial, bottom-tuples all a-initial; empty tuple only diagonal); base order discrete. Mismatch p=(a^2b,a), q=(ba^2,a): p<=q in T(C) componentwise via generator + reflexivity, but p is not a D-generator bottom (second component 'a' never of form a^n b) and D has no chains, so p not<=q in D; comparison c identity bijective monotone but not order-iso. Additivity lemma a^{m+n}b=a^m(a^n b)<=a^m(b a^n)=(a^m b)a^n<=(b a^m)a^n=b a^{m+n} uses only contexts+transitivity, sound; hence {lam2,lam3} entails all lam_n (semigroup <2,3> covers all n>=2). Machine rerun of verify.py confirms A,B,D1,D2,E. Q=<a,b|all lam_n> therefore isomorphic to finite presentation <a,b|lam2,lam3>; no rank jump. Side glosses about Q underlying poset and strong finitariness are imprecise but do not enter headline proof.
